C-UPDATER-STATS.Name: Update funnel counters: feed checks, Update-button clicks and update successes counted at our own gateway — no identifiers, redirect-only
C-UPDATER-STATS.Summary: Today the update funnel is invisible: the desktop updater fetches a single static manifest straight from GitHub Releases (tauri.conf.json:80-82, https://github.com/xronocode/mark/releases/latest/download/latest.json), and GitHub's per-asset download counters are the only signal — noisy, without history, and unable to separate the Windows installer's update-clicks from site downloads at all. This change adds a tiny redirect-only counting gateway on our own domain (updates.mark.xronocode.com, a Cloudflare Worker whose code lives in the repository and whose deployment is owner-executed): the updater's check endpoint becomes https://updates.mark.xronocode.com/feed?from={{current_version}}&os={{target}} (Tauri substitutes the placeholders itself) with the current GitHub URL kept as the second fallback entry; the release feed's platform artifact URLs are composed through https://updates.mark.xronocode.com/pkg/{platform}/{version} so every updater artifact fetch — an Update-button click — is counted and separated from site downloads. The gateway records one aggregate datapoint per request (event, day, OS, from-version/platform/version) into Workers Analytics Engine — three months retention, no IPs, no user agents, no identifiers of any kind — and immediately 302-redirects to the deterministic GitHub URL it derived itself; it never synthesizes or proxies manifest bodies and never reflects request input into a redirect target (not an open redirector). A small owner-run query script turns the data into day-by-event-by-OS tables; update successes need no new client code at all — a success is simply the appearance of from={new version} in later checks. MAS builds are untouched (their config strips the updater); the C-UPDATER-ROLLBACK restore paths keep their direct GitHub fetches and are not counted.

Problem.Description: (1) We cannot answer the owner's standing question (owner, 2026-10-28, translated from Russian: "how many clients clicked the Update button, and how does that differ from plain downloads"). The updater's only observable footprint today is GitHub asset download counters: approximate, scanner-noisy, no per-day history, and structurally unable to split Windows update-clicks from website downloads because the same Mark_{ver}_x64-setup.exe serves both (research session 2026-10-28: on macOS the updater-only .tar.gz gives a usable proxy — 39 clicks vs 44 site .dmg downloads at v2.8.2 by day 4 — but Windows mixes both into one counter, and the feed checks themselves are invisible). (2) The research session already settled the approach: count at the server side on our own domain — a «counter on the door» that sees who came in but identifies no one — using Tauri's officially supported endpoint placeholders ({{current_version}}, {{target}}, {{arch}}; v2 updater docs) so every check carries its origin version, and routing the updater's artifact fetches through distinct URLs so button clicks separate from site downloads by construction. No in-app telemetry is needed or wanted: the app has none, its CSP forbids renderer egress, and its privacy posture (no analytics in the app, documented on the site privacy page) stays intact. (3) Anything we build must not become a reliability or trust liability: the updater's function must survive a gateway outage (hence the fallback endpoint kept), the manifest must never be synthesized by our code (hence redirect-only), and the artifact trust anchor stays the minisignature against the app-pinned key — the same anchor the forward updater and the C-UPDATER-ROLLBACK restore already use — so an indirection in the URL changes nothing about what is trusted.

Goals.R-1: Counting gateway (M-069 mt-stats-gateway): a Cloudflare Worker in tools/stats-gateway/ (worker.mjs + wrangler.toml + README) bound to updates.mark.xronocode.com, deployed owner-side via wrangler. Two routes only: /feed (count event=check with day/os/from derived from the Tauri placeholders, then 302 to the GitHub latest.json manifest; os validates against its own two-entry OS table — {darwin, windows}, exactly the values the {{target}} placeholder substitutes per the v2 updater docs — NOT the /pkg platform table) and /pkg/{platform}/{version} (count event=pkg, then 302 to the deterministic GitHub release asset derived from strictly validated path segments — darwin-aarch64 → Mark_{ver}_aarch64.app.tar.gz, windows-x86_64 → Mark_{ver}_x64-setup.exe, both under the v{version} release). Every redirect Location is derived from validated inputs, never reflected; unknown or malformed routes get a plain 404 with no datapoint and no redirect. The worker is redirect-only by construction: no route ever returns a body it made. Request semantics are pinned: GET only; route and platform matching is exact and case-sensitive with no trailing-slash or percent-decoding tolerance; /feed counts only when exactly the two expected parameters are present and valid — os validated against the OS table above ({darwin, windows}, the values {{target}} actually produces) and from against strict semver — a bare /feed, extra parameters, or any other method is a 404 with zero datapoints, so scanner traffic can never pollute the numbers.
Goals.R-2: Client check endpoint: tauri.conf.json plugins.updater.endpoints becomes exactly two entries — the gateway feed URL with placeholders (https://updates.mark.xronocode.com/feed?from={{current_version}}&os={{target}}) first, the current GitHub latest.json URL second. Tauri continues to the next entry only on a non-2XX answer, so a gateway outage silently degrades to today's behavior (function preserved, stats undercounted); a 302 that resolves 200 counts as success and never falls through. The pubkey, installMode and everything else in the updater block are untouched.
Goals.R-3: Counted artifact URLs: the release pipeline's feed composition (.github/workflows/release.yml latest.json platform fragments) points each platform's url field at the gateway (https://updates.mark.xronocode.com/pkg/darwin-aarch64/{ver} and /pkg/windows-x86_64/{ver}) instead of the raw GitHub asset, so updater artifact fetches are counted at the gateway while site/cask downloads keep their direct GitHub links. Consequence pinned honestly: because every client — including already-shipped ones — reads whatever latest.json the newest release publishes, click coverage begins with the first release carrying the new manifest; check coverage begins only when clients run a build with the R-2 config. The signature fields in the manifest are untouched, and the trust anchor stays the app-pinned minisign key: the URL was never the anchor (the same argument the C-UPDATER-ROLLBACK restore relies on).
Goals.R-4: Data shape and privacy: one Workers Analytics Engine datapoint per gateway request — index=event (check|pkg), blobs={day, os, from} for checks and {day, platform, version} for pkg fetches. No IP, no user agent, no cookie, no unique or stable identifier of any kind is read or written; Cloudflare's implicit edge metadata (request.cf, CF-IPCountry, geo/ASN) is never read; the gateway stores nothing else. Day buckets are UTC. Retention is Analytics Engine's own three months (documented limit); no long-term warehouse is built. Expected volume is tens of events per day against the 100k/day free write quota — orders of magnitude of headroom, and a write failure must never affect the response (the datapoint is fired via waitUntil and the redirect always returns).
Goals.R-5: Query tooling: tools/stats-gateway/query.mjs — an owner-run script (CF_API_TOKEN in the environment) that queries the Analytics Engine SQL/GraphQL API and prints day × event × OS/platform tables with from-version breakdowns, plus the update-success reading (a success is the appearance of from={N} in checks after N shipped; no client change exists or is needed) and the honest downloads reading: plain downloads stay GitHub-counter-derived (roughly the asset total minus pkg counts, noisy, no history) — the gateway answers the Update-click half exactly and the plain-downloads half only as that derived approximation, stated plainly in the README. A fixtures-driven dry mode (no network) validates the script's output shape in CI; the script never attempts to reconstruct anything finer than counts.
Goals.R-6: Privacy surface (mark-site, local repository, deploy is the owner's separate flow): the privacy page is amended so that every network-activity statement on it remains true — the opening "no analytics, no telemetry" framing (scoped honestly: the app contains no analytics code; its update check itself lets the gateway count aggregate daily statistics, disclosed in the list), the update-check destination sentence (checks now go to updates.mark.xronocode.com first, which counts and redirects to GitHub), the "complete list" framing, and the "What we collect / no servers that receive data from the app" paragraph (our gateway receives aggregate daily counts: event, OS/platform, version, nothing else) are all reconciled with the new reality, plus the counting disclosure itself (aggregate daily numbers, version and OS only, no identifiers, three-month retention, scoped to the download edition — store builds ship no updater). The app itself still contains no analytics and its CSP still forbids renderer egress.
Goals.R-7: Unaffected by design: app-store builds (their overlay strips the updater entirely), the C-UPDATER-ROLLBACK paths (its Windows restore keeps its two direct deterministic GitHub fetches — restore traffic is recovery, not funnel analytics — and its macOS restore is offline), the Homebrew cask and website download links (direct GitHub, uncounted), and the updater's signature scheme.
Goals.R-9: Owner decision gate — RESOLVED 2026-10-29: the owner ordered the spec and plan passes with the full review protocol (owner, 2026-10-29, translated from Russian: "can you make the detailed plan with the four-corner review and two clean review passes?"). The four-corner gate over this spec (two consecutive clean passes — rounds 5-6 of the ReviewLog in design-context.xml) completed before this approval; the plan pass records the same instruction as its approval basis once its own gate is clean. Execution and deployment wait for a separate owner order.
Goals.R-8: Governance: new governed module M-069 mt-stats-gateway (SCRIPT role, MAP_MODE LOCALS) owning worker.mjs, wrangler.toml and query.mjs with a V-M-069 verification anchor (unit pins + dry-run commands); the in-file VERSION + CHANGE_SUMMARY bump in the one touched governed file that carries them (the release.yml feed composition block); the tauri.conf.json endpoints edit is strict JSON and carries no in-file markers, so its record lives in this change's graph/verification bundle instead; deployment is owner-executed and documented (wrangler deploy steps in the README) — no credentials or CI deployment in this change, and no release authorization is implied by merging it.

Constraints.Item: Language: every committed artifact is English; the owner's request of 2026-10-29 (translated: "can you make the detailed plan with the four-corner review and two clean passes?") is cited in translation with speaker and date as the instruction for this spec+plan pass.

No product code beyond configuration: the only client-side change is the tauri.conf.json endpoints array; the renderer, the Rust modules and the updater plugin are untouched. No new client dependency of any kind.

Redirect-only, derived-target-only: no route returns a synthesized body, and no redirect target is ever built from unvalidated input (strict platform/version validation; anything else 404s without a datapoint). The gateway must not be usable as an open redirector.
Counting is best-effort: an Analytics Engine write failure or quota error must never change the response — the redirect (and the fallback story) always holds.
No identifiers, ever: no IP logging, no user-agent recording, no cookies, no per-install IDs, no cross-session correlation. Counts are day × event × OS/platform/version only.

Reliability floor: the updater must keep working when the gateway is slow, wrong or gone — the GitHub endpoint stays as the second entries-array fallback, and the R-3 manifest change keeps every URL resolving to the same GitHub bytes.

The release pipeline edit is code-in-scope but action-out-of-scope: release.yml changes ship in this change's PR, while running a release, publishing anything, or deploying the worker remains behind the separate owner release workflow (and wrangler deploy is owner-executed).
Existing gates stay green and unweakened: npm test, cargo test, renderer suites, release-tauri dry-run lane, grace lint current with no new errors beyond the recorded baseline.
Four-corner review with two consecutive clean passes over this spec (recorded in design-context.xml) precedes owner approval; the plan pass repeats the gate before execution is proposed.

NonGoals.NonGoal: Any in-app telemetry, analytics SDK, or renderer network egress — the app keeps zero analytics; only the server-side gateway counts.
A dashboard UI, scheduled reports, or alerting — the owner-run query script is the whole reporting surface.
Per-user, per-device or per-install measurement; cohort reconstruction; anything finer than aggregate counts.
Long-term storage beyond Analytics Engine's three-month retention (an export pipeline can be a future change if the rolling window proves too short).
Staged rollouts, kill-switches or feed content logic — the gateway redirects; it never decides what a client gets.
Counting or altering the C-UPDATER-ROLLBACK restore fetches; counting website/Homebrew downloads; touching the App Store edition.
Automated worker deployment from CI (credentials stay owner-side); any release/tag/publication activity.

Implementing any R-item, deploying the worker, or running any release — this pass produces the spec and the plan; plan.xml exists beside this spec after its own gate, and execution waits for a separate owner order.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Gateway behavior: /feed with valid placeholder parameters (os strictly darwin or windows — the {{target}} substitution) records exactly one check datapoint (index event, blobs day/os/from) and 302-redirects to the GitHub latest.json URL; /pkg/{platform}/{version} with a valid platform and strict-semver version records exactly one pkg datapoint and 302-redirects to the deterministically derived GitHub asset URL; malformed versions, unknown platforms, unknown paths, unexpected query input and any non-GET method get a plain 404 with zero datapoints and zero redirects; every Location header in every test is a derived GitHub URL (no reflected input anywhere).

Best-effort counting: when the Analytics Engine binding errors or is absent, every route still returns its redirect/404 exactly as with it (write failures are swallowed inside waitUntil; response latency and status are datapoint-independent).

Client config: tauri.conf.json updater endpoints list exactly the gateway feed URL with exactly the two placeholders ({{current_version}}, {{target}}) verbatim followed by the current GitHub URL; the pubkey and installMode are byte-unchanged; mas builds register no updater plugin and perform no updater network activity; the rollback module's windows_release_base URLs stay byte-unchanged (restore traffic never touches the gateway); released updater versions are always strict x.y.z, so the gateway's strict-semver validation never 404s a real release (the repo's versioning today is strict-only and the rollback module's own strict_semver already assumes it).

Feed composition: release.yml's latest.json platform fragments point url at the gateway pkg routes for darwin-aarch64 and windows-x86_64 with the release's own version, while signature fields and the feed's schema stay byte-compatible with the current updater (an old client consuming the new manifest downloads through the gateway and verifies against the same pinned key).

Query tooling: query.mjs in dry mode (fixtures) prints the day × event × OS/platform table and the from-version breakdown without any network access; in live mode it reads only CF_API_TOKEN from the environment and prints the same shape; the README documents the success-reading (from={N} appearing after N shipped), the three-month window, that day buckets are UTC, and the downloads-vs-clicks reading (plain downloads remain the GitHub-counter-derived approximation: asset total minus pkg counts).

Privacy: every network-activity statement on the mark-site privacy page remains true after the edit — the update-check destination, the complete-list framing and the "what we collect / no servers" paragraph are reconciled with the gateway reality, and the aggregate-counting disclosure (event, OS/platform, version only, no identifiers, three-month window) is present; the app contains no new renderer egress and no analytics (pinned by a source scan in tests; the updater's check/download destination changes per R-2/R-3 by design).

Deployment story: the README lists the owner-executed wrangler deploy steps and the route (updates.mark.xronocode.com/*) with the AE binding and workers_dev disabled (the gateway answers on exactly one host); no credentials, tokens or account identifiers are committed.

Governance: M-069/V-M-069 routed in the same bundle as the code with content-free markers where the house style expects them; VERSION + CHANGE_SUMMARY bumps land in every touched governed file; npm test, cargo test, the release-tauri dry-run lane and grace lint (target, then final with --run-commands) stay green against the recorded baseline (the lane builds the app and proves no breakage; the manifest shape itself is pinned by the static fragment tests, not by the lane — the first live proof is the owner-gated release); the change's ReviewLog (design-context.xml) shows two consecutive clean four-corner passes before approval was requested, and the plan's ReviewLog shows the same before execution is proposed.

AffectedAreas.Item: tools/stats-gateway/ — new governed SCRIPT module M-069: worker.mjs (routes, validation, AE write via waitUntil, redirects), wrangler.toml (route updates.mark.xronocode.com/*, workers_dev disabled, Analytics Engine binding), query.mjs (dry/live aggregate tables), README (deploy steps, success reading, retention window, the downloads-vs-clicks reading); tests under tests/tools/stats-gateway.test.mjs.

vitest.config.ts — the include pattern grows tests/tools/**/*.{test,spec}.{js,ts,mjs} so the gateway tests actually run under npm test and the explicit vitest invocation (today the include covers only src/renderer and tests/renderer).
tests/renderer/release-preflight.test.js — its exact single-element endpoints pin (line ~241) becomes the two-entry expectation: gateway feed URL first, the current GitHub URL second.
src-tauri/tauri.conf.json — the updater endpoints array only (gateway feed URL with placeholders + GitHub fallback).
.github/workflows/release.yml — the latest.json platform-fragment url fields (gateway pkg routes); nothing else in the pipeline changes.

mark-site (separate local repository, no remote by design) — the R-6 privacy-page amendment: the opening framing, the update-check destination sentence, the complete-list framing and the what-we-collect paragraph reconciled, plus the counting disclosure.
.grace/graph/* and .grace/verification/* — M-069/V-M-069 routing in the same bundle as the code.
Explicitly untouched: src/renderer/** and src-tauri/src/** (no product code), the updater pubkey, the rollback module's fetch URLs, the cask and website download links.

VerificationIntent.ExpectedCommand: npx vitest run tests/tools/stats-gateway.test.mjs && npm test && cargo test --manifest-path src-tauri/Cargo.toml && grace lint --path . --change C-UPDATER-STATS --assertions final --run-commands (exact suites fixed by the approved plan; worker live behavior additionally proven by the owner-executed deploy checklist)
VerificationIntent.ExpectedEvidence: Unit pins for both routes: correct derived Location headers (including the strict platform/version derivation table), 404-without-datapoint for every malformed input class, zero reflected input in any Location (open-redirect guard), datapoint shape (index event, blob keys) asserted against a fixture binding, and best-effort counting (binding failure does not change any response). Static pins: tauri.conf.json carries both endpoints with the placeholders verbatim and an unchanged pubkey; release.yml feed fragments carry gateway URLs; a renderer source scan proves no new egress/analytics. Dry-mode output-shape test for query.mjs. Governance: M-069/V-M-069 routed, headers bumped, lint clean against the baseline. The live proof (a real check and a real pkg fetch appearing in the query output) is owner-executed after deployment and recorded as pending evidence, mirroring the C-UPDATER-ROLLBACK protocol pattern.

Assumptions.Assumption: Facts verified while drafting (2026-10-29): the updater feed is a single static GitHub URL (tauri.conf.json:80-82) and the pubkey/installMode sit unchanged beside it; Tauri v2 officially substitutes {{current_version}}, {{target}} and {{arch}} in endpoint URLs and continues to the next endpoints entry only on a non-2XX answer (v2 updater docs, verified 2026-10-28); Workers Analytics Engine stores data for three months (AE limits page, fetched 2026-10-29) and the Workers free plan caps 100k requests per day (each gateway request writes at most one datapoint, so the request cap is the operative quota — orders of magnitude above the expected tens of events per day); the GitHub latest.json manifest lives at releases/latest/download/latest.json and release.yml composes its platform fragments with per-release asset names (verified in the C-UPDATER-ROLLBACK wave); the updater verifies artifact minisignatures against the app-pinned key, so URL indirection does not touch the trust anchor.

the xronocode.com zone is DNS-managed in Cloudflare (C-22: a DNS-only CNAME mark -> xronocode.github.io; the site itself is served by GitHub Pages per C-64 D-1 — a Cloudflare hosting move remains a future decision), so an updates.mark.xronocode.com Worker route with an Analytics Engine binding is zone-level configuration the owner can perform; deployment runs owner-side with the owner's wrangler credentials — no account access is assumed available to automation.

Coverage ramps honestly: check counting starts with the first released build carrying the R-2 config; pkg counting starts with the first release publishing the R-3 manifest (which every client, old or new, then reads). Until then the GitHub counters remain the only signal. No shipped client is modified retroactively.

Change states as checked while drafting: active bundles are C-47, C-50, C-PAGE-WIDTH-TABLES; C-UPDATER-STATS collides with no active or archived id; C-UPDATER-ROLLBACK is archived applied (its restore keeps direct GitHub fetches — this change deliberately does not count them). All states are re-verified at plan time.
